uncertainties: Every questionnaire response is a simulation; the sources establish policies and principles rather than 240 literal personal answers.

State constitutions, municipal taxation, recall, digital surveillance, drug policy and private sexual arrangements include institutional or rights-based inference where no direct personal answer is available.
Brain implants, enhancement genetics, cultivated meat, personal rural-versus-urban preference and space priorities are hypothetical inferences; mixed compound claims can be neutral.
Older abortion, marriage and religion statements establish personal positions; the 2024 religious-discrimination report describes proposals, not enacted legislation.
Defence spending percentages use different accounting conventions; the profile relies on the direction of increased capability rather than equating differently defined percentages.
distinctions: Likely nearby social democrats include Obama, Trudeau and Starmer; Albanese specifically combines managed migration, public industrial investment and AUKUS with multiculturalism and renewable electricity.
Free trade coexists with domestic industrial and fuel-security support.
Catholic background coexists with secular civil equality; nuclear-submarine support coexists with opposition to the proposed domestic nuclear-electricity program.

Reviewed other close stored models: Støre has estrutura 33.8 and tecnologia 66.2 versus Albanese 48.6 and 52.4; Mattarella has moral 57.5 and religiao 43.8 versus 76.4 and 56.0. Australian federal coordination, regulated technology and documented civil-equality policies support retaining this independent profile despite aggregate similarity.

similarityReview.reason: Distinct people with plausible overlap in regulated markets, civil equality and alliances. In the stored vectors, Albanese has economia 66.3 versus Obama 55.0, reflecting public Medicare and strategic public investment; poder 59.1 versus 46.2 reflects firearms and online safeguards; imigracao 34.3 versus 25.0 combines multiculturalism with managed skilled migration. This compares the existing model, not a claim that every inter-person difference is a measured historical fact. All 240 answers were authored independently and none was changed to manufacture separation.

The added Gillard model is a distinct Labor career with plausible overlap. Gillard explicitly describes herself as atheist, emphasises equivalent roles for public and private providers, and combines national-security diplomacy with alliance deployments. Albanese differs in the stored model on religiao (56.0 versus 63.1), economia (66.3 versus 60.3) and intervencao (43.6 versus 30.5). These are editorial model distinctions, not measured historical distances. Existing Albanese answers are unchanged.

These are different social-democratic leaders with shared welfare, market and equal-rights principles. Scholz’s Länder-focused federalism scores more decentralised than Albanese’s national-standards approach; regulated cannabis access and Germany’s NATO/sanctions role give different liberty and external-engagement results. Scholz’s explicit non-affiliation differs from Albanese’s Catholic upbringing and public-life account. The closeness is retained, not edited away.
